id_convention.depth_rule: Maximum 3 levels. All content deeper than subtopic belongs in wiki_content array.

sources_field.scope: Optional on any subtopic. Expected on all ALE-LAWS subtopics and any subtopic with node_type: code_provision.

structure.label: Human-readable name for the source
structure.url: Direct URL to the document or official page — set to TBD until verified

difficulty_values.1: Foundational — straightforward recall; first-time takers should answer correctly
difficulty_values.2: Standard — requires understanding; typical ALE item difficulty
difficulty_values.3: Advanced — requires application or analysis; distinguishes topnotchers
difficulty_values.4: Expert — multi-step reasoning or rare tested provision; high discriminating power

id_convention.three_d_lab_linked_note: Boolean. True if a 3D Lab interactive module exists or is planned for this subtopic. Primarily relevant for ALE-STRC, ALE-MATL, ALE-UTIL, ALE-DSGN topics requiring spatial comprehension.
id_convention.prerequisite_note: Array of subtopic_ids that should be mastered before this subtopic is introduced in the Camp Trail. Empty array means no enforced prerequisite.

wiki_items_field.scope: Replaces wiki_content strings with typed structured objects. wiki_content retained for backward compatibility — treat as deprecated.

structure.type: One of: heading | fact | definition | formula | code_provision | detail | exam_tip | cross_ref | warning
structure.source_ref: Optional subtopic_id of the ALE-LAWS node that governs this provision

type_values.heading: Section header within wiki_items — renders as subsection title
type_values.formula: Numeric formula, dimensional value, or calculation
type_values.code_provision: Direct citation of law provision, section, or dimensional requirement
type_values.detail: Sub-item or elaboration of the preceding item — renders indented
type_values.exam_tip: ALE exam strategy, frequency note, or study guidance
type_values.warning: Critical correction, common error, or important distinction

exam_structure.administered_by: Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) & Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture (PRBoA)
exam_structure.frequency: Twice a year (typically January and June)

cross_reference_subject.name: Philippine Laws & Codes for Architectural Practice
cross_reference_subject.note: Study subject only — law questions appear distributed across Areas A, B, and C. This subject provides a unified cross-reference index.

exam_structure.passing_threshold: General weighted average of 70%, with no subject below 50%
exam_structure.experience_requirement: 2 years of Diversified Architectural Experience (DAE) under a Registered Architect

subjects.description: Analysis of architectural manifestations from the beginning of civilization to contemporary periods. Covers factors affecting architectural style (historical, environmental, socio-cultural), general characteristics, structural and decorative contributions, and notable examples — with emphasis on Philippine architectural legacies, preservation, and the Pillars of Philippine Architecture.

wiki_content: Equilibrium — sum of forces and moments equals zero; basis for all structural analysis
Free Body Diagrams — isolating structural elements to visualize forces
Hooke's Law — stress proportional to strain within elastic range (σ = Eε); defines material behavior under load
Modulus of Elasticity (E) — material stiffness; steel ~200 GPa, concrete ~25 GPa, wood ~10 GPa
Yield Point — stress at which permanent deformation begins; design stays below this
Ultimate Strength — maximum stress before fracture
Stress Types: Tension (pulling), Compression (squeezing), Shear (sliding), Torsion (twisting), Bending (tension + compression)
Moment of Inertia (I) — resistance to bending; depends on cross-section shape; deeper sections resist more
Section Modulus (S = I/c) — cross-section efficiency in bending; architects choose sections with higher S for stronger beams
Deflection limits — L/360 for live load, L/240 for total load; ensures serviceability

subtopics.subtopic_name: DepEd Order No. 66 s.2012 — School Building Design Standards
wiki_content: === GOVERNING INSTRUMENT ===
DepEd Order No. 66, Series of 2012: Revised Guidelines on the Design and Construction of School Buildings
Administering agency: Department of Education (DepEd), in coordination with DPWH for public school buildings
DPWH Standard Designs: DPWH issues standard school building designs used in government contracts; provides reference dimensions used in ALE Area C problems
=== STANDARD CLASSROOM DIMENSIONS ===
DepEd standard classroom area: 7.0m × 9.0m = 63 sq.m. (this is the most-tested value)
Standard capacity: 45 students per classroom
Area per student: 63 ÷ 45 = 1.4 sq.m./student (net classroom area)
Minimum ceiling height: 2.7m (naturally ventilated); 2.4m (air-conditioned)
=== BUILDING CONFIGURATION ===
Single-loaded corridor preferred (classrooms on one side, corridor facing courtyard/open air)
Double-loaded corridors allowed but require mechanical ventilation for inner classrooms
Typical floor-to-floor height: 3.3–3.6m for standard DepEd buildings
Maximum floors: 3 stories for standard DepEd Type buildings; 4+ stories require special structural design and elevator
=== ORIENTATION AND DAYLIGHTING ===
Classrooms face north or south (Philippines is in northern tropics; north-facing minimizes direct solar glare on learning boards)
Long axis of classroom building oriented east-west to maximize north/south window exposure
Window area: minimum 10% of floor area (per NBC Rule VII); DepEd prefers 15–20% for natural daylight
Cross-ventilation: windows on at least two sides; high-placed windows on north wall for exhaust ventilation
=== CIRCULATION AND EGRESS ===
Corridor width: minimum 2.0m (clear); 3.0m preferred for high-traffic school corridors
Stairway width: minimum 1.5m (2× NBC minimum) to handle student rush between periods
Maximum travel distance to exit: 30m per NBC (unsprinklered educational occupancy)
Ramps: required at all level changes for BP 344 compliance; 1:12 maximum
=== SANITARY FACILITIES ===
Toilet blocks at each floor level; separate male/female
Ratio: 1 toilet per 30 students (DepEd standard); NBC ratio = 1 WC per 25–30 students depending on sex
Drinking fountains: 1 per 75 students (DepEd guideline)
Janitor's closet with mop sink on each floor
=== SPECIAL EDUCATIONAL ROOMS ===
Science laboratory: minimum 90 sq.m. (2× standard classroom); lab tables 760mm × 1500mm; gas, water, electrical services at benches
Computer laboratory: minimum 70 sq.m.; raised access floor for cabling; air-conditioned; 1 computer per 2 students minimum
Library/Learning Resource Center: minimum 115 sq.m. for standard public school; shelving density: 1 shelf unit per 10 students
Home economics room: 80–90 sq.m.; kitchen equipment; good ventilation; gas connections
Industrial Arts/TLE room: 90–100 sq.m.; higher ceiling (3.6m) for equipment; strong power supply
=== SITE PLANNING REQUIREMENTS ===
Minimum school site area: 3,000 sq.m. for elementary (DepEd standard); 4,000 sq.m. for secondary
Flag ceremony area: minimum 3 sq.m. per student; paved or lawn; facing east
Play area: minimum 2 sq.m. per student outside building footprint
Parking: 1 slot per classroom (faculty/staff); separate student drop-off from staff parking
=== STRUCTURAL REQUIREMENTS ===
All public school buildings must comply with NSCP 2015 seismic design (Zone 2)
DPWH Type I school building: single-storey; CHB walls; RC frame
DPWH Type II: two-storey; RC frame with CHB infill
Elevated water tank: required on site for water independence during supply interruptions
=== EXAM NOTE ===

ALE Area C school design problems typically give lot dimensions, student population, and grade level. Compute: (1) number of classrooms from enrollment ÷ 45, (2) AMBF from lot analysis, (3) required circulation areas, (4) toilet counts. The 7×9m classroom is the anchor dimension — know it cold. Orientation (north/south-facing) is consistently a judgment question in Area C.
